```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = getwd())
```

This analysis explores our miscalibration issues with Replogle rd7 by comparing to Velten's analysis.

```{r libraries, echo = FALSE}
library(sceptre)
library(ondisc)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(patchwork)
```


```{r data-import, echo=FALSE}
repl_offsite <- paste0(.get_config_path("LOCAL_REPLOGLE_2022_DATA_DIR"))

# Load original sceptre object (without cell cycle scores)
import_dir_original <- paste0(repl_offsite, "processed/rd7/")
our_sceptre_object <- read_ondisc_backed_sceptre_object(
  sceptre_object_fp = paste0(import_dir_original, "sceptre_object.rds"),
  response_odm_file_fp = paste0(import_dir_original, "gene.odm"),
  grna_odm_file_fp = paste0(import_dir_original, "grna.odm")
)

# Load our sceptre object with cell cycle scores
import_dir_cell_cycle <- paste0(repl_offsite, "processed/rd7/with-cell-cycle/")
our_sceptre_object_cell_cycle <- read_ondisc_backed_sceptre_object(
  sceptre_object_fp = paste0(import_dir_cell_cycle, "sceptre_object.rds"),
  response_odm_file_fp = paste0(import_dir_cell_cycle, "gene.odm"),
  grna_odm_file_fp = paste0(import_dir_cell_cycle, "grna.odm")
)

# Load crispat/Velten sceptre object
crispat_sceptre_object <- readRDS("~/data/external/braunger-2024/sceptre_object_RPE1.rds")

# Set path for cell cycle analysis results
sceptre3_rd7_offsite <- paste0(.get_config_path("LOCAL_SCEPTRE3_DATA_DIR"), "replogle-2022/rd7-cell-cycle/")
```

# Sceptre Object Comparison

Let's first compare our `sceptre_object` to Velten's:
```{r object-comparison}
crispat_sceptre_object
our_sceptre_object
```

The main differences are that 

1. they have way fewer cells, 
2. they have 17 fewer NT gRNAs, and 
3. they have extra covariates `G2M_score` and `S_score`, which encode cell cycle state. 

The first is largely irrelevant to us because what we care about are the cells with NT gRNAs only, and so we don't care about the other cells anyways. An inspection of Velten's codebase revealed that they retained all cells with NT gRNAs, *except* those containing 17 NT gRNAs found by Replogle to have apparent effects on genes. This brings us to difference 2, which is very important. Throwing out NT gRNAs with an apparent effect on genes prior to a calibration check is circular reasoning, so we would want to repeat the calibration check with all NT gRNAs. Item 3 may be important; if the cell cycle state acts as a confounder. Let's check whether this is the case in the next section.

# Cell Cycle Effects on Non-targeting gRNAs

Cell cycle state is known to impact gene expression; let's check based on Velten's data whether it also impacts which gRNA a cell received.

```{r cell-cycle-nt-grnas, echo = FALSE}
nt_grnas <- crispat_sceptre_object@grna_assignments$indiv_nt_grna_idxs |> names()

velten_df <- crispat_sceptre_object |> 
  get_cell_covariates() |> 
  select(S_score, G2M_score)
velten_df$grna <- character(length = nrow(velten_df))

for(nt_grna in nt_grnas){
  velten_df$grna[crispat_sceptre_object@initial_grna_assignment_list[[nt_grna]]] <- nt_grna
}

velten_df <- velten_df |> filter(grna != "")
```

```{r}
aov(S_score ~ grna, data = velten_df) |> summary()
aov(G2M_score ~ grna, data = velten_df) |> summary()
```

We see that both cell cycle variables are correlated with gRNA, which makes cell cycle a possible confounder. Maybe controlling for cell cycle is enough to explain the miscalibration we're seeing. 

# Calibration Check with Cell Cycle Scores

We can't rely on the Velten data to get the cell cycle scores for our calibration check, since they excluded 17 gRNAs. Therefore, I added functionality to `ondisc` to calculate cell cycle during import (which I hope will be independently useful). Below is a check that the cell cycle scores I computed from scratch match those from the Velten data, for the cells that overlap. 

```{r cell-matching, echo = FALSE}
# Examine covariate data frames to understand structure
crispat_covariates <- crispat_sceptre_object |> get_cell_covariates() |> as.data.frame()
our_covariates <- our_sceptre_object_cell_cycle |> get_cell_covariates() |> as.data.frame()

# Identify shared covariates
shared_covariates <- intersect(names(crispat_covariates), names(our_covariates))

# Cell matching function
create_matching_key <- function(covariate_df, shared_cols) {
  if(length(shared_cols) == 0) {
    stop("No shared covariates found for matching")
  }
  
  # Round numeric columns to avoid floating point precision issues
  key_df <- covariate_df[shared_cols]
  numeric_cols <- sapply(key_df, is.numeric)
  key_df[numeric_cols] <- lapply(key_df[numeric_cols], function(x) round(x, 6))
  
  # Create composite key
  apply(key_df, 1, function(row) paste(row, collapse = "_"))
}

# Create matching keys for both objects using only response covariates
matching_covariates <- c("response_n_nonzero", "response_n_umis")
crispat_keys <- create_matching_key(crispat_covariates, matching_covariates)
our_keys <- create_matching_key(our_covariates, matching_covariates)

# Find matches
matches <- match(crispat_keys, our_keys)
valid_matches <- !is.na(matches)

# Create mapping data frame
cell_mapping <- data.frame(
  crispat_idx = seq_along(crispat_keys),
  our_idx = matches,
  matched = valid_matches,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Filter to only matched cells
matched_cells <- cell_mapping[cell_mapping$matched, ]

# Extract unique matches only
unique_matches <- matched_cells[!duplicated(matched_cells$our_idx), ]
```

```{r cell-cycle-correlation, echo = FALSE}
# Compare cell cycle scores for uniquely matched cells
crispat_indices <- unique_matches$crispat_idx
our_indices <- unique_matches$our_idx

# Extract cell cycle scores
crispat_g2m <- crispat_covariates$G2M_score[crispat_indices]
crispat_s <- crispat_covariates$S_score[crispat_indices]
our_g2m <- our_covariates$response_g2m_score[our_indices]
our_s <- our_covariates$response_s_score[our_indices]

# Create comparison data frame
cell_cycle_comparison <- data.frame(
  crispat_G2M = crispat_g2m,
  our_G2M = our_g2m,
  crispat_S = crispat_s,
  our_S = our_s
)

# Calculate correlations
g2m_cor <- cor(crispat_g2m, our_g2m)
s_cor <- cor(crispat_s, our_s)

# G2M score scatter plot
g2m_plot <- ggplot(cell_cycle_comparison, aes(x = crispat_G2M, y = our_G2M)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = "y~x", color = "red", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = paste("G2M Score Comparison (r =", round(g2m_cor, 3), ")"),
    x = "Crispat G2M Score",
    y = "Our G2M Score"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1)

# S score scatter plot
s_plot <- ggplot(cell_cycle_comparison, aes(x = crispat_S, y = our_S)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = "y~x", color = "red", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = paste("S Score Comparison (r =", round(s_cor, 3), ")"),
    x = "Crispat S Score",
    y = "Our S Score"  
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1)

# Display plots side by side using patchwork
g2m_plot + s_plot
```

The agreement seems pretty good. I then reran the calibration check using this newly imported data on a million negative control pairs, with the same formula (and other analysis parameters) used by Velten. 

```{r calibration-plot, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("~/data/projects/sceptre3/replogle-2022/rd7-cell-cycle/plot_run_calibration_check.png")
```

Unfortunately, the miscalibration remains. Below is a table of how the false positives are distributed across gRNAs:

```{r worst-offenders, echo = FALSE}
calibration_results <- readRDS(paste0(sceptre3_rd7_offsite, "results_run_calibration_check.rds"))
calibration_results |> 
  filter(significant) |> 
  count(grna_target) |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  print(n = 20)
```

So we have about 20 NT gRNAs that make up the bulk of the problem; likely these contain the 17 filtered out by Replogle and Velten.

# Conclusion

Adding cell cycle didn't resolve the calibration issue, leading me to believe that the Replogle data simply have NT gRNAs that "didn't work", in the sense that they do have effects on some genes. In my opinion, this means that the Replogle data are too low-quality for us to analyze.
